question: The Regional Government of Castile-La Mancha has launched a prior consultation period for a rare earths research permit application entitled ‘Neodimio’ (Neodymium) in an area bordering the Special Protection Area of Áreas Esteparias del Campo de Montiel (ES0000158).

It should be noted that, on 7 January 2021, the High Court of Justice of Castile-La Mancha rejected a previous similar project for the exploitation of rare earths by the same developer and in an area very close to that of the current project and, as such, also adjacent to the Natura 2000 site in question.

This judgment is significant as it established that mining activity could also have negative repercussions when carried out in areas close to Natura 2000 sites, on the basis that it would seriously impact the connectivity between protected and affected areas. In view of this: 1.

Does the Commission consider that the Spanish authorities have failed to comply with the Habitats Directive (Directive 92/43/EEC) by declaring this new project admissible, given that a similar project from the same developer was rejected by means of the aforementioned national judgment?
In view of the above information, what action will the Commission take?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.5.2024) The Commission is not informed of this project, and therefore, it is not in a position to assess if the authorities have failed to comply with the Habitats Directive1. The Habitats Directive does not preclude, in principle, mining activities.

However, it establishes a stepwise procedure under Article 6(3) to prevent the authorisation of plans and projects with negative effect on Natura 20002. The Commission has issued guidance on the implementation of this provision3 and on ‘undertaking non-energy extractive activities in accordance with Natura 2000 requirements’4.

Without prejudice to the Commission’s role as guardian of the Treaties, Member States are primarily responsible to ensure compliance with EU law. In parallel, the Commission prioritises its enforcement efforts on cases pointing to a systemic breach of EU law5.
Due to the individual nature of the case and in view of the national judicial precedent, the Commission considers that this matter can be best addressed at national level.
1 Council Directive 92/43/EEC on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and flora, OJ L 206,

22.7.1992, p. 7–50. 2 Without prejudice of Article 6(4). 3 https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/99a99e59-3789-11ec-8daf-01aa75ed71a1/language-en 4 https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/69b6d6c1-bfc1-4fe5-9252-08af20a95cfe/ 5 As set out in the Communication of 19 January 2017 (EU law: Better results through better application C/2016/8600, OJ C 18, 19.1.2017, p. 10–20) and in the Communication of 13 October 2022 COM(2022) 518 final - Enforcing EU law for a Europe that delivers.
